history.name: Glass Beach
history.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Project asset: square equipable creature background for the Critters mobile game.
Input image 1 is the current background to redesign and the authoritative ART STYLE reference. Rebuild its scenery and composition substantially as specified; preserve its thick BLACK cartoon outlines, rounded simple forms, broad flat color areas, restrained two-tone cel shading, and friendly hand-drawn game-world style. Outline major foreground and midground shapes boldly in real near-black, about 6–10 px at a 1536 px canvas. Do not drift into painterly realism, soft edge painting, intricate textures, or hairline outlines.
Deliver one clean 1536 x 1536 square opaque background, full bleed. No character, animal, creature, UI, lettering, labels, watermark, border, or built-in character shadow.
GAME COMPOSITION: The game crops away the upper 39% in its wide view, so the scene's identifying shapes must read within y=42–78% of the square, not only in the sky. It may crop the sides on narrow stages too. Reserve the lower central area x=32–68%, y=75–98% as a visually calm continuous flat standing surface, with feet at y=93%. Keep depth/landmark shapes behind that space. The eventual creature is about 20% of image width, so ordinary pebbles, flowers, loose debris, and other small objects must remain genuinely tiny. No giant decorative items. Keep clean separate silhouettes suitable for later light animation.
REDESIGN GLASS BEACH: Replace the tropical golden-sand cove composition with a distinctive open, cool-toned sea-glass shoreline. Silvery mauve-gray sand, gentle dusky aqua sea, and a sweeping curved/diagonal tideline from middle-left into the right midground. Use an open distant horizon and a few low dark slate shelves on one side, rather than enclosing cliffs and large green bushes on both sides.
The defining feature is several graceful ribbons of SMALL rounded frosted sea-glass pebbles washed up along the tideline and side edges: mint, teal, lavender, pale blue and a little amber. Their collective colored bands should be recognizable at thumbnail size. Each actual pebble is only about 8–18 px on a 1536 image, many separated tiny chips grouped into simple color patches, never large jewel boulders or crystals. Leave the central bottom standing patch mostly plain gray sand with very few small chips. A thin scalloped foam curve and a broad band of wet reflective sand should make an asymmetric shoreline shape visible in the bottom 60% of the artwork. Soft cool morning light, not a golden tropical cove. Avoid flashy sparkles, glass monoliths, oversized pebbles, seashells, buildings, and trees. Preserve strong black contours on slate, shore and wave shapes.

history.name: Glass Beach
history.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this Glass Beach image, keeping its exact square composition, camera, ocean, slate rock positions, silver-mauve sand, curved shore and open lower central standing space. Make only these finishing adjustments: reduce EVERY colored sea-glass pebble/chip to 40% of its current linear width and height, including the side clusters and bottom corners, without shrinking or moving any actual gray slate boulders. Repaint exposed space with matching sand. Preserve the sweeping collective sea-glass bands by distributing the smaller chips naturally within the same side areas; individual chips should read as tiny bits no larger than 12–18 pixels on a 1536 canvas, not gemstones or colorful cobbles. The large waves and rock landforms should have strong clean BLACK cartoon outline contours about twice the current weight, matching the earlier game art's bold inked look. Preserve simple flat color, no extra texture or busy detail. Do not enlarge the glass to make it visible: visibility comes from the grouped color bands. No giant gem, shells, characters, text, border, sparkle effects or shadows from an absent character. Keep full-bleed square opaque art and the plain central foreground.

history.name: Snow Ghost Ridge
history.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine only the SNOW-COVERED TREE FORMS in this Snow Ghost Ridge cartoon background. Preserve the exact camera and square composition, black outline thickness, open snowy foreground, distant mountains, sky, cliffs, pale blue-white palette, and lighting. Currently the snow-covered trees still have ordinary triangular Christmas-tree silhouettes and tiers of branches. Replace those silhouettes with true wind-sculpted SNOW GHOSTS: irregular rounded asymmetrical rime-coated natural tree pillars, thick curved knobby lobes swept sideways by wind, blunt bent tops, no visible needle branches, no tidy triangles or stacked branch skirts. They should resemble dense smoothly rounded white natural snow sculptures with only two-tone blue shadow patches, boldly black outlined, clearly different from conventional pine trees. Keep the existing cluster footprint and comparable heights, with the smaller midground snow ghosts fully visible in y=45–76% so they remain recognizable when the top is cropped. These are buried trees, NOT characters: absolutely no faces, eyes, mouths, limbs or anthropomorphic shapes. Keep the lower center x=32–68%, y=75–98% clear for a creature. No added objects, text, border, character, intricate icy texture, or photorealism.
